text: uracil), and FAP (fluorouracil, doxorubicin, cisplatin), have not proved more effective than fluorouracil alone.8,9 However, there is evidence5,15 that gemcitabine can produce slightly better survival than fluorouracil in patients who can toler- ate it, and it has been recommended as the standard of care.1,5,8,9,16 There is also some evidence that its effective- ness may be improved if it is given at a fixed dose rate of 10 mg/m2 per minute, rather than by conventional infu- sion.5,14 Gemcitabine has also been investigated in combi- nation with other drugs such as cisplatin, docetaxel, iri- notecan, oxaliplatin, or capecitabine, as well as with newer targeted therapies such as bevacizumab, cetuximab, trastu- zumab, or erlotinib.5,14,17 A meta-analysis13 found a sur- vival benefit for gemcitabine-based combination therapy compared with gemcitabine alone. Combinations showing benefit in terms of progression-free survival or overall sur- vival include gemcitabine with capecitabine (GEMCAP), cisplatin (GEMCIS), oxaliplatin (GEMOX), or erlo- tinib.5,6,14,18 The combination of cisplatin, epirubicin, fluorouracil, and gemcitabine (PEFG) has also shown im- pressive results.14 Rubitecan is one of many other antineo- plastics under investigation for advanced pancreatic can- cer,12,14 and other therapies that have been investigated include somatostatin analogues, other hormonal strategies, and biological therapies.19 A preliminary study suggested that flutamide (an anti-androgen) might be beneficial20 but flutamide with gemcitabine proved of no more benefit than gemcitabine alone.21 Pancreatic cancer vaccines are also under investigation.6,17 1.
